description:
The generic domain vocabulary a repository needs to be usable is a package directory in this repository, so it reaches an adopter as declared content rather than as compiled-in bytes.

## Background

The configuration a fresh repository receives today is rendered from a compiled template: a four-level type hierarchy, seven label namespaces, six item-kind declarations, a validation strictness and default type name, and a documentation-area classification carrying this repository's own development areas. Four of the five classes the boundary names appear in it literally.

All of it is declarable. The contribution vocabulary already reaches the hierarchy, the namespaces, the item kinds and the strategic types; the documentation and validation targets are added by the work this depends on. What remains is to author the package: a manifest declaring that content, with no assets of its own.

Its item-kind set is the whole vocabulary. A kind is registry-first over a registry file, and a package may not name a source file no repository has — but two of the three registries already exist in a freshly initialized repository, one seeded and one empty, and the third does not only because initialization never creates it. That asymmetry is about the scaffolder rather than about the kind, so initialization creates the third registry the way it creates the empty one, and the vocabulary is declared whole. The workflow package then contributes its own entries into that registry instead of publishing the file over it.

One detail is decided here rather than discovered. The scaffold's commented coordination guidance renders two engine constants into prose. A package is bytes, so a packaged copy of that comment cannot be a projection of them; the comment drops its numbers rather than carrying a hand-maintained copy of two defaults.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A package directory in this repository declares the type hierarchy, the label namespaces, the item kinds, the strategic types, the validation defaults, and the documentation-area classification a repository needs to be usable.
- [hard] REQ-02: It declares every item kind a freshly initialized repository can carry, and no kind whose source file no repository has.
- [hard] REQ-03: It carries no asset and no workflow content: no gate, no template, no rule encoding an opinion about how work is sequenced.
- [hard] REQ-04: Applying it to a bare repository yields a configuration equivalent to what the scaffold writes today, apart from the guidance comment's rendered constants, which it states without numbers.
- [hard] REQ-05: The package validates as a package and reports a stable content address.
- [hard] REQ-06: Initialization creates the invariant registry the way it creates the gate registry — present and empty — so a repository declaring no invariant still resolves the kind, and a repository declaring one needs no package applied first.
- [hard] REQ-07: The workflow package contributes its invariant entries into that registry rather than publishing the registry file, so applying it to an initialized repository does not depend on the file being absent.

## Notes

Nothing is removed from the binary here. The compiled template is deleted by the work that can prove this package replaces it.
title: Assemble the default vocabulary as a package
